pairs.question: Quid tu, malum, me sequere?
pairs.answer: Quia certumst mihi, quasi umbra, quoquo tu ibis te semper sequi.
pairs.derivation: Olympio asks Chalinus why he follows him; Chalinus answers that he is resolved to follow him everywhere like a shadow. Answer ends at the first full stop ('sequi'); what follows ('Quin edepol etiam, si in crucem uis pergere...') is further elaboration, cut. Inline verse line-breaks joined into running text; no words added or reordered.

pairs.question: Quicum litigas, Olympio?
pairs.derivation: Lysidamus asks with whom Olympio is quarrelling; Olympio answers 'with the same one as always (i.e. your wife).' Dropped the preceding separate question 'Quid istuc est?' from the speaker's line so the extracted interrogative is the one actually answered. Answer is the complete reply sentence; the following 'Cum uxore mea?' is a new question.

pairs.question: Quid agit? quid loquitur tecum?
pairs.answer: Orat obsecrat ne Casinam uxorem ducam.
pairs.derivation: Lysidamus asks what she does and says to Olympio; Olympio answers that she begs and beseeches him not to marry Casina. Answer ends at the first full stop; the following 'Quid tu postea?' is a new question. Verse line-break joined; no words altered.

pairs.question: Quid eius uxor? ubi erit?
pairs.answer: Mea uxor uocabit huc eam ad se in nuptias, ut hic sit secum, se adiuuet, secum cubet.
pairs.derivation: Olympio asks about Alcesimus's wife and where she will be; Lysidamus answers with the plan that his own wife will summon her to the wedding to keep her here. Skipped the non-answering preamble 'Lepide repperi' (a lead-in 'I've found a clever solution') and started at the operative answering sentence; ended at its first full stop ('cubet'), before 'Ego iussi...'. Verse line-breaks joined; no words added or reordered.
